title: Standard Chartered CEO calls for AI guardrails, says human judgment remains key to jobs
key_facts: Standard Chartered Group CEO Bill Winters spoke to CNA on 9 Oct 2026 at the Milken Institute Asia Summit in Singapore.
He called for stronger regulation and international cooperation on AI: 'I can think of very few industries that have needed regulation more than this one.'
He said it takes three years to get a new aspirin formulation through regulators, 'but we have not put any guardrails on AI'.
He said US-China rivalry plus AI risk makes cooperation as important as, maybe second to, nuclear weapons.
He warned cybercriminals could use AI to breach security; 'some bad things will happen'.
The bank has automated almost 25 per cent of its earlier roles, yet headcount has increased; about 85 per cent of displaced staff were reskilled.
Roles needing human judgment or interaction, such as wealth-management relationship managers, will stay important.
quote_evidence: I can think of very few industries that have needed regulation more than this one.
People still trust people, and it's going to be a long time before we trust the machine over the person.
why_it_matters_hint: A major bank chief calls for AI rules while saying the bank has grown headcount despite automating a quarter of roles.
notes: Direct interview in CNA's own reporting. Staffing figures are the bank's own, as told by its CEO.
